detail: Initial preparation assumed Org3–Org5 training files lived under full_v2. Existing sealed prediction provenance points to full_org3/4/5_v1. Preparation now derives the TRAIN file from its accepted VAL source directory; first failed attempt wrote only the preserved metadata snapshot.
Best-local selection is stored as the string graphsage, not a dictionary. Corrected only the new reporting reader; accepted selections unchanged.

Older calibration subgroup masked counts include outside-subgroup rows. New tables separately report original masked-inside-population and outside-population. Detection counts and accepted summaries are unchanged.

Initial PR/ROC rendering used a staircase convention inconsistent with AP/trapezoidal ROC depiction. Final PR uses pre-step endpoint precision, ROC linear interpolation. Source numeric curves/metrics unchanged; draft images retained and figure_manifest_v2 identifies final figures.

Artifact exporter saved both workbook drafts then exited -1073740791. Final v2 independently verified: ZIP, all 58,578 source cells, 12 cached formulas and 21 native tables pass. Initial formatting draft v1 preserved.

Draft every observed attacking address is not an oracle authorization. Accepted baseline shares suspicious IPs only after actual local alerts using observed recent evidence; paper must describe this non-oracle rule.

VAL contains zero wholly locally-undetected campaigns; cannot demonstrate federated rescue of that empty subset. Formal DP, federation, poisoning robustness, integrated ledger costs and held-out performance remain untested.

Five simulated partitions of synthesized web authentication data are not independent real owners or cyber-physical deployment evidence. Measured CPU end-to-end latency does not establish a production sub-50/100-ms SLA.
